extractor.note: Whole file grep-scanned for the theme's search terms plus 'Wesensschau', 'free variation', 'immutable', 'innate', 'residuum' and 'simple nature'; none of the last six occur in the sections read. Closely read § 9 (lines 89-110) and § 13 (151-160).

coverage_note: Covers § 9 (empirical and a priori attitude; ontology of nature and formal ontology) and § 13 (the resolvability of the connection of res cogitans and res extensa; the distinctio phaenomenologica) in full. §§ 1-8, 10-12 and 14 onward were keyword-scanned only.

units.claim: The empirical and the a priori attitude are distinguished by what comes to givenness in each: existence-objectivities in the one, essence-objectivities in the other.
units.quote: In the one, existence-objectivities come to givenness; in the other, *essence*\-objectivities — in the one, nature; in the other, ideas.

units.claim: A marginal note is reported to label the attitude in which numbers and the like are given, as no things and no facts of nature, the eidetic attitude.
units.quote: (A marginal note labels this the *eidetic attitude*.)

units.claim: A complete exclusion of every existence-positing is required in order to grasp the a priori, the ideal essences, in their existence-purity.
units.quote: in order to grasp the apriori, the ideal essences, in their existence-purity

units.claim: It is said not to belong to the essence of a thing that it is a sensing thing, so that a thing's being a body is a facticity.
units.quote: It does not belong to the essence of a thing that it is, so to speak, a *sensing* thing

units.term: essence of the cogitatio / essence of the extensio
units.claim: The essence of the cogitatio and the essence of the extensio are said to have, in principle and as essences, nothing to do with one another.
units.quote: The essence of the *cogitatio* and the essence of the *extensio* have, in principle, *as essences*, nothing to do with one another.

units.claim: The commentary calls this the phenomenological transformation of Cartesian dualism: not a metaphysical claim that two substances exist but an eidetic claim that the two essences are mutually independent.
units.quote: not a metaphysical claim that two substances exist, but an *eidetic* claim that the essence "consciousness" and the essence "thing" are mutually independent

units.claim: Not all necessity in the realm of experience is essence-necessity, since otherwise all the natural sciences would be a priori sciences.
units.quote: Hence not all necessity in the realm of experience is *essence*\-necessity — otherwise all the natural sciences would be apriori sciences.

absences.expected_because: This section rewrites Cartesian dualism as a thesis about the mutual independence of two essences, and names res cogitans and res extensa throughout - so if any commentary in the corpus were to connect Husserl's Wesen to Descartes' doctrine of natures, this is the section where the connection would be made.
absences.note: The sharpest negative result for gap-007 in this pass: the Cartesian vocabulary that is taken up here is res cogitans and res extensa, and what is taken from it is a distinction of essences, never the doctrine of vera et immutabilis natura or of innate ideas.
